clue.text: A chorister not involved in the arrangement

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer in the choir sits out a musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' signals the anagram of A CHORISTER NOT; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestration is the scoring of music for an orchestra, a kind of musical arrangement.

clue.text: Winding up very rich when in it

definitions.meaning: coiling something into a cylinder, as with a carpet
the idiom '... in it' means having lots of money

explanation.surface: Someone is making a fortune just as their business is being wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling up a rug winds it up, and someone 'rolling in it' is wealthy.

clue.text: A measure of concealment

definitions.meaning: an old English unit of land area
a hiding place, as birdwatchers use

explanation.surface: A suggestion of how much secrecy is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: The hide was an old land unit, and a hide is also a screened shelter for watching wildlife unseen.

clue.text: It's true I will appear in the screen version

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A claim that a story is authentic, with someone appearing in its film adaptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges I plus SCREEN; 'It's', 'will appear in the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and heartfelt, the sense of true in 'a true friend'.

clue.text: Comes to life again and gets out of bed

explanation.surface: A sleepy person revives and finally climbs out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is both to be resurrected and to get up after sleep.

clue.text: Spell it out to me

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the two letters of it are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A request to have something spelled out clearly to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns IT into TI, followed by ME; 'to' is a link. 'Spell' looks like the spelling verb but is the noun for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period, as in 'a spell abroad', a stretch of time.

clue.text: Theatrical gentleman to rise with a greeting

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word to is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hello is a common greeting

explanation.surface: An actor gets up to say hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns TO into OT in this down clue, then HELLO; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the title figure of Shakespeare's play, a character of the stage.

clue.text: One does not wish one's children to be brought up in it

definitions.text: One does not wish one's children to be brought up in it

parts.words: One does not wish one's children to be brought up in it
parts.note: 'brought up' reads as raised, but here means appearing before a judge, in a court for young offenders

explanation.surface: A parent's thought about the wrong place to raise a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that tries young offenders is where a child would be 'brought up' to face charges.

clue.text: It cuts both ways

parts.note: the idiom for something with good and bad effects, read literally as a blade sharp on each side

explanation.surface: A remark that an argument has consequences on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade honed on both sides literally slices in either direction, and the phrase means an advantage that can also harm.

clue.text: Led a nun astray, but not charged!

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A man leads a nun into sin but faces no charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges LED A NUN; 'but' is a link. 'charged' suggests a criminal charge, but means loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Unladen means carrying no load, so not charged in the sense of not loaded up.

clue.text: Possibly show me love in one way or another

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may be arranged some other way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A plea to a partner to show some affection however they can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges SHOW ME plus O. Love as O comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Somehow means by some means not specified, which is doing it one way or another.

clue.text: It's about time to revise

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for time is read backwards

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide

explanation.surface: Someone decides the moment has come to make changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TIDE to give the answer; 'It's' and 'to' are links. TIDE meaning time survives in 'time and tide' and Eastertide.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct and rework it, which is revising it.

clue.text: Having little to say about trees

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of trees are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is reticent on the subject of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse person uses few words, being brief and curt in speech.

clue.text: A helpful guide, or hint, left inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter for left is placed within the word for hint

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint

explanation.surface: Advice on useful pointers, with something left in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts L within CUE; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a piece of evidence that guides someone towards an answer.

clue.text: Lengthy communication?

parts.note: suggests a long message, but means a message sent along a long wire, the wire also being a nautical unit of length

explanation.surface: A question about a rambling letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by telegraph wire was called this, and the same word names a long rope and a sea measure.

clue.text: One making up for lack of practice

definitions.text: One making up for lack of practice

parts.words: One making up for lack of practice
parts.note: 'lack of practice' sounds like being rusty, but means a medical practice short of its doctor

explanation.surface: Someone compensating for being out of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in doctor or cleric fills the gap when a practice is without its regular one.

clue.text: He doesn't appreciate where the coal goes

definitions.meaning: into a fireplace grate, read as two words

explanation.surface: A man who takes his coal fire for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person shows no thanks, and coal is put on the fire grate.

clue.text: Stretch a point and look inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for look sits within the word for point

parts.note: a prong is one sharp point of a fork
lo is an old word meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Someone exaggerates and peers into the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places LO within PRONG; 'and' is a link. 'Stretch a point' looks like an idiom but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something is to lengthen it, drawing it out in time.

clue.text: A deerstalker's comedown?

parts.note: comedown suggests a hunter's disappointment, but the deerstalker is a cap whose side pieces come down

explanation.surface: A hunter of deer suffers a humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: The flaps on a deerstalker hat fold down to cover the ears.

clue.text: Is it for the fleet-footed?

parts.note: fleet-footed suggests runners who rush; the reading plays on rush as hurry and as a reed woven into floor covering

explanation.surface: A question about something for fast runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor covering woven from rushes shares its first word with hurrying.

clue.text: Fix old boy up with dummy pill

parts.note: to place something is to fix it in position

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the abbreviation for old boy is read from bottom to top

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a former schoolmate with a fake tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses OB to BO in this down clue; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert tablet given in trials, a pretend medicine.

clue.text: Arched and jumped

definitions.meaning: having a curved roof like a crypt
leapt over, as with a pole

explanation.surface: Someone curved their back and leapt.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved ceiling is described as such, and a gymnast who leapt over a horse did this.

clue.text: Beggar gets state hand-out

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
a grant is money handed out

explanation.surface: A homeless person receives government money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state hand-out' reads as welfare but splits into VA and GRANT; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a homeless wanderer, often reduced to begging.

clue.text: One who cheats in pontoon?

parts.note: a cheat is called a ..., and in the card game pontoon a player asking for a card face-up says 'twist'

explanation.surface: A question about a card sharp at the pontoon table.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game blackjack, where to 'twist' is to take another card.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is called a twister, and in pontoon a player who says 'twist' takes another card.

clue.text: Love to operate on the river

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
to use a machine is to operate it

explanation.surface: Someone loves running a boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'on the' are links. The Ouse is a name shared by several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a name borne by several English waterways, such as the one through York.

clue.text: Vehicle to travel as freight

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A lorry travelling as goods transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by ship or plane, which is freight.

clue.text: We four are coming back to have a look

indicators.note: coming back means the whole run of letters is read from right to left

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four friends return to take a look at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are coming back' turns WE plus IV into the answer; 'to have a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a sight or glance, so having a view is having a look.

clue.text: It isn't all go

definitions.meaning: a portion rather than the whole

explanation.surface: A remark that life is not all action.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is less than the whole, and to depart is to go away.

clue.text: The advantage being sharp gives one?

definitions.meaning: the upper hand over a rival
a sharp blade has a keen cutting side

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether quick wits give you the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand is having this, and anything sharp has a cutting one.

clue.text: Storm about like a politician in a tantrum

definitions.text: like a politician in a tantrum
definitions.meaning: on the warpath; the word also contains MP within a word for tantrum

explanation.surface: An MP throws a fit and storms around.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, which an MP in a rage might do.

clue.text: His examinations necessitate a lot of book-work

definitions.text: His examinations necessitate a lot of book-work

parts.words: His examinations necessitate a lot of book-work
parts.note: suggests a student's revision, but the books are a company's accounts being checked

explanation.surface: A student facing exams has much reading to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who inspects a firm's financial records is this inspector.

clue.text: Modern painting's condition

definitions.meaning: read literally, the status of the art world or of a picture

explanation.surface: A comment on the condition of contemporary painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the latest technology, and read literally it is how art stands.
